correctness.rationale: Over R=k[t]/(t^m), the centralizer is End_{k[t]}(R⊕k), and the induced action on the quotient by t is triangular with diagonal a(0),d. Nilpotence is equivalent to their vanishing: in that case X² sends the module into t times the module, so X^{2m}=0. Products of nilpotent companions yield only the antisymmetric off-diagonal-coefficient determinant in the top-left commutator, equivalently rank at most one on the two rows. Comparing gX with X'g gives the simultaneous action (b,c,z)↦(λb,λ⁻¹c,z+αc+βb), with all lower coefficients unchanged and all three parameters freely realizable. A zero row pair is fixed. A nonzero pair determines one line; normalized coefficients on it have two axis types or q−1 nonzero-product types, with q−1 representatives each. The translation orbit is exactly the q-vector affine line in the top coefficient space, leaving q^{r−1} cosets. Thus the stated numbers and sizes follow and sum to the raw tuple count. For the reduced variety the unrestricted coefficients split off; the rank-one charts of the determinantal factor are smooth of dimension r+1, it is geometrically irreducible by outer-product parametrization, and the vanishing linear parts of all minors give a 2r-dimensional tangent space at zero, singular for r≥2. The proof also works for m=2, when there are no lower coefficients, and in characteristic two.
residual_risks: The supplied checker was inspected rather than replayed. It uses the derived action in coordinates, so the independent direct multiplication check supplements rather than repeats it.
Geometric conclusions are for the reduced variety, not an arbitrary nonreduced presenting scheme.
